history.note: Looks back 14 days at each listed wallet's first buys of a token and reads what traded in the minute after. Move = from the price paid one or two blocks behind the wallet to the price about 10 s later, before our own fees; "won" = better than +3%. Good = not a bot, 30+ buys, and passing (half or more won, average above +3%) on BOTH the older and the newer half of its buys. History is not a live fill: a lead to test, not proof.

slow.note: Paper and read-only. CANDIDATES: the listed wallets, the busiest pump.fun buyers, and (day holders) wallets that bought 0.2+ SOL of coins that keep trading for days (3+ days old, no stables or staked SOL: on 12 of Jupiter's lists, or verified with $50000+ traded in a day; and coins our wallets traded on 3+ days), sampled at 0.25 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 13 days back, 3 pages each. A full first page inside 3 h = bot; 10+ trips in its newest 200 transactions with a median hold under 10 min = fast (flipper); neither is read further. A wallet read in full that neither passes nor is near (10+ trips, median hold 30+ min, ahead) keeps its numbers but not its swaps and is read again every 14 days; passing and near ones daily. SCREEN: each candidate's own SOL swaps over the last 30 days as round trips (first buy until 90% sold). Passes = not a bot, 20+ trips, first sell a median 30+ min after its first buy, realised SOL positive in BOTH halves of the period, 40%+ won, no single trade half or more of the profit. Realised SOL is before network fees. LATE: for its newest 30 trips, a copier entering 30 s / 5 min after its first buy and selling 30 s after its first sale, priced from other people's trades, 1% cost taken off: an estimate (a late price over 5x off the wallet's own is left out). NOT COPYABLE: a passing wallet with 15+ late copies checked and fewer than 1 in 5 won; it is not followed. smallStartPct = trips whose first buy was under half the wallet's usual. PAPER: followed wallets copied live with 0.25 SOL at Jupiter quotes, 5 s / 30 s / 5 min / 30 min after we see the buy, sold 5 / 30 s after its first sale (or at 72 h); by wallet, in5s is the entry a real copy makes; proven = followed now, and of its newest 40 closed 5 s copies 20+ priced, half or more won, ahead; provenThen = closed 5 s copies by whether their wallet counted as proven when the copy was bought (from its copies closed by then); crowd = closed 5 s copies by how many other followed wallets had bought the coin before and not yet sold; crowdOnePerCoin = that as a rule at one copy a coin (a copy taken when minOthers+ others hold the coin and none of ours is out), newer = its newer half; top5Sol = SOL made by the five best copies (most of the net = a few big winners, not a rule). Every transaction is simulated on the chain before it is sent. dryRun / dryRunLong: an open order of ours simulated, hourly until it passes and then daily; dryRunClose / dryRunCloseLong: a close order simulated against a position that exists on the chain. leverage.note: PAPER. Every closed rule trade scored at each leverage with $20 of collateral: result = leverage x the trade's result after fees and borrow; a trade whose price went against it by more than (1 / leverage - fees - 0.2%) at any hourly candle while it was open is LIQUIDATED and loses all its collateral. Confidence is a score 0-4 fixed when the trade opens (7-day trend agrees, 30-day trend agrees, copied traders lean the same way, quiet market) and sets leverage 1.5, 2.5, 4, 6.5, 10x. PAPER. tradersUse is the leverage the copied traders had SET on the positions we copied (Hyperliquid's number; their real exposure can be lower when they keep spare cash). tiers scores each closed copy at every leverage with $20 collateral, asTheTrader at the trader's own setting. Each entry is sold as soon as it is up 10% after costs, else 60 s after its own purchase (holdOnly = no target, just the 60 s). priceVsFastestPct = how much more (+) or less (-) that entry paid than the instant quote (median). risingPct = share of buys where it paid more.

walk.note: Paper. Only buys known since 2026-11-11T16:15:00.000Z (after the pace rule was written), 0.25 SOL each, bought the moment we know, sold at +10% or after 30 s (t30) and 60 s (t60). t60sl10 / t60sl15 / t60sl20 = the 60 s rule, sold sooner at the first check (2, 5, 10, 20, 30 s) where the copy is 10% / 15% / 20% down (the real test looks every 0.75 s, so it stops sooner and more often than this). late1... = the same rules bought 1 s after we know, nearer to where the real test's buy lands (its gap is still the one of the moment we know). calm = the trader had bought fewer than 3 times in the 3 hours before; gap = how far our price already was above the wallet's.

hours.note: Paper, every stored buy. By the hour of the day in KST (3 hour blocks): the copy sold at +10% or 60 s, bought the moment we know (t60), bought 1 s later (late1t60, about where the real test lands) and that with a 15% stop. days = on how many different days the block has buys: one day is not a pattern.

repeats.note: Paper, every stored buy. first = no other listed wallet bought the coin in the 30 min before; second = one other did; third or later = two or more did. Same three ways of buying as in hours.

secondWave.note: Paper, every stored buy whose window was checked to the end. Buy the coin entrySec after a listed wallet bought it, if no other listed wallet bought it in between (at the sale price of that moment plus the coin's own in-and-out cost, fees included; a model, not a quoted buy). Sell 2 s after the next listed buy of the coin (withNextAt5: 5 s after), or endSec after the first buy if none comes. buyers = how many listed wallets had bought the coin in the 30 min up to that buy. firstHalfAvgPct / secondHalfAvgPct = the average of the earlier and of the later half of the copies: a pattern should show in both. nextPct = how often the next buyer came in time. waitSecMedian = from our buy to it.

buySize.note: Paper, every scored buy, split by the size of the wallet's buy: against its usual buy (the median of its 5+ earlier buys, no hindsight) and in SOL. Holdings are not recorded, so "share of the wallet" cannot be read. Buys under 0.1 SOL were never recorded. late1 = bought 1 s after we knew (where the real test landed), +10% or 60 s; late1x30 = 1 s late, sold at 30 s; instant = the moment we knew (faster than real), +10% or 60 s. Real = the real test's sent copies matched to their buy; "won" = came back with more SOL.

sameBlock.note: What if we had landed right behind the wallet: entry at the price the first followers really paid in its block or the next (where none, the wallet's price +2%), same exits. An estimate, kept apart from the real rules.

traders.note: A trader's record = every first buy of that wallet we saw, copied on paper the moment we knew and sold at +10% or 30 s. From 4 copies on: good = made money on average and half or more won; bad = lost on average and fewer than half won; mixed = between. Few copies make a noisy verdict: the rules copy-d0-trader-* judge each buy only on the copies before it.
